problem: Prior LLM-based planners on scene graphs (SayPlan, MoMaLLM) rely on heavy LLMs or paid APIs (GPT-4/4o), which are costly and impractical for edge devices, and off-the-shelf inference gives no control over travel distance or number of retrials.
motivation: Edge robots have limited memory (about 6GB) and energy, so small language models (<=4B params) are needed, but pretrained SLMs produce badly formatted outputs and weak planning. The paper observes that LLM teacher supervision combined with simulator feedback can transfer reasoning while also shaping efficiency factors like distance.
key_idea: Train small language models for scene-graph-based sequential object-search planning by interleaving LLM-teacher SFT distillation with PPO reinforcement learning driven by simulator rewards (executability, exploration, distance penalty, format).
insight: SFT alone already transfers most of the LLM's reasoning (Table 2: SFT-only SR 85-91%), while RL adds control over side factors: doubling the efficiency penalty from 0.3 to 0.6 (RL-SFT+) cuts distance (e.g. Llama-3 17.65 to 9.69) at the cost of SR. Removing the few-shot SFT format stage makes RL training unstable, and OOD text-game evaluation shows the tuned SLMs keep their general reasoning, so they are not overfit.
method: Scene graph to text: Build a Hydra-style Navigation Voronoi Graph, split it into room subgraphs at doorways, and form a two-level (room/object) scene graph serialized as text; the LM classifies room types and receives the previous action.
Action space and CoT prompting: The LM outputs analysis, reasoning and one command from navigate, go_to_and_open, close, explore and done, in a chain-of-thought format following MoMaLLM.
Stage 1 few-shot SFT: LoRA fine-tuning for 3 epochs on 500 offline teacher (GPT-4o) responses to teach output format and give a strong prior for later RL.

Stage 2 interleaved RL-SFT: For each task, run the SLM, execute its actions in the simulator, do a PPO update on the reward, then an SFT cross-entropy step on the teacher LLM's answer to the same prompt.

Reward design: r_success=5 on done() with goal visible; otherwise the sum of executability (±0.3), exploration (0.1 x new Voronoi nodes), efficiency (distance penalty, 0.3, or 0.6 for RL-SFT+) and format penalty (-0.1).
Small models: Qwen-2.5 3.1B, Llama-3 3.2B and Phi4-mini 3.8B, 4-bit quantized (Unsloth), about 4GB memory, LoRA, learning rate 1e-5.

setting.backbone: Phi4-mini 3.8B / Llama-3 3.2B / Qwen-2.5 3.1B (LoRA fine-tuned, 4-bit); GPT-4o as teacher
setting.training_data: 8 iGibson train scenes with simulator rollouts; 500 offline GPT-4o responses for stage 1; GPT-4o teacher answers online in stage 2
setting.observation: text-serialized hierarchical scene graph (rooms and objects) plus Voronoi graph from simulator, previous action
setting.action_space: discrete high-level commands: navigate, go_to_and_open, close, explore, done
setting.privileged: perfect localization and simulator-provided object visibility/scene information; GT scene graph from simulator

numbers.eval_set_note: 7 test scenes x 25 runs = 175 episodes, randomized start poses/targets/object distributions

numbers_note: The MoMaLLM GPT-4o baseline has SR 97.14, SPL 65.92, Dist 18.01, Retrials 0.39 (baseline, not included). OOD text-game results appear only in a figure.
results: SmallPlan's Phi4-mini (3.8B) reaches SR 96.57% and SPL 70.41% with Dist 16.13, close to GPT-4o MoMaLLM in SR (97.14%) and better in SPL (65.92%) and distance (18.01). Fine-tuning improves every SLM strongly over its pretrained version (e.g. Llama-3 SR 53.68 to 93.14).
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation (iGibson) with perfect localization and simulator-provided perception; no real-robot tests
Models around 1B are insufficient (Llama-3 1B reaches only 51.42% SR), and hyperparameters and epochs are set by trial and error
The distance penalty trades off success rate (SLMs terminate early), and SFT uses only teacher outputs without ground-truth labels
